articleTitle: Implementation of the SMART Method and Location Based Service Technology in a Sewing Service Search Application
abstract: The tailoring business involves services where tailors create or repair clothing. Currently, the number of tailors with various skill sets is on the rise. However, customers often struggle to find tailors who meet their specific needs. They have to spend time visiting tailor shops, just to assess whether a tailor is a suitable match or to place an order, even when the distance and location are uncertain. This inefficiency hampers the process. In this rapidly advancing technological era, many businesses leverage technology to promote their services, including the tailoring industry. To address this issue, the author aims to develop an Android-based Tailor Locator Application that utilizes Location Based Services (LBS) and the SMART Method. This application will utilize LBS technology to display the distance and location between customers and tailors, while continuously updating the location information of both customers and tailors. The application will also implement the SMART method to rank tailors based on ratings and provide tailor recommendations.

articleTitle: Detection of Drug Effects on Brain-Based EEG Signals using K-Nearest Neighbours
abstract: Drugs are very harmful to the body, especially to the performance of the brain, which causes brain damage. Several methods for drug detection, especially in medical, have been done, but using non-medical technology is still rare. This study proposes drug detection using an EEG system with a KNN classifier. In the experiment, 20 subjects in one of the prisons in West Java were involved. Extraction and classification results using K-NN with 96% accuracy were obtained. These results show the potential of the proposed technology for drug detection.

articleTitle: Enhancing Tilapia Fish Farming Through IoT-driven Monitoring and Automatic Feeding Technology
abstract: Aquaculture of tilapia fish is a popular venture due to high market demand. To ensure successful farming in aquariums, maintaining optimal water conditions is crucial. The recommended pH range is 6.5-8.5, and water turbidity should be carefully controlled to avoid excessive pollution. Deviations from specified values necessitate water replacement. Feeding tilapia requires careful consideration, with portions ranging from 3-5% of their body weight. This study aims to enhance tilapia farming practices by leveraging evolving technologies. Monitoring water pH, and turbidity, and controlling feeding based on nutritional requirements and weight can prevent overfeeding and optimize resource utilization. During a monthlong monitoring period conducted every three days, turbidity ranged from 5 to 25 NTU, with pH levels stable at 7.0 to 7.7 (2% error rate). In the control group, an Efeeder system provided feedings three times daily at 50 g per meal for 100 fish, resulting in a 3% error rate in feed weight. This research provides valuable insights for fish farmers seeking to improve their tilapia farming practices.

articleTitle: Classification of Pneumonia Using a Deep Learning Convolutional Neural Network
abstract: An acute lung disease diagnosed by examining white spots on X-ray results is called Pneumonia. However, based on several evaluation results by doctors, those white spots occasionally lead to other lung diseases such as Tuberculosis (TBC). The data-driven approach for computer-aided diagnosis can be one of the innovative solutions to help classify the types of pneumonia that attack the lungs. This research utilizing Deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) algorithm to classified Xray images with several models namely GoogLeNet, ShuffleNet V2, and a model designed by the author. From 5,856 data of Xray image results, GoogLeNet was able to detect the accuracy of 74.9%, ShuffleNet V2 was 76%, and the Convolutional Neural Network model that the author designed was 79.8% with the fastest training time than the other models.

articleTitle: Vehicle Accident Detection System with LPWAN Technology for Information Transmission
abstract: This system is designed to monitor vehicles and provide information about their position and movements, par- ticularly in the event of an accident. The system can detect factors that commonly contribute to accidents, such as changes in speed, tilting, and collisions. The data is collected from three types of sensors: the ADXL 345 accelerometer, the tilt sensor, and the crash collision sensor. The system uses LoRa communication technology, which is affordable and easy to implement. To test the system's performance, LoRa modules were tested under two conditions: Line of Sight (LOS) and Non-Line of Sight (NLoS). The tests used a spreading factor between 10-12 and a bandwidth of 125 kHz and 250 kHz. The results showed that the data from the sensors accurately reflected the measurements taken by the transmitter device on the receiver device.

articleTitle: Designing an Autonomous Qibla Finder Mobile Robot Utilizing the Second al-Biruni's Method from Kitab Tahdid Nihayat al-Amakin
abstract: This research explores the utilization of the second al-Biruni's method to determine Qibla direction in the design of an autonomous Qibla finder mobile robot based on an Arduino microcontroller, GPS module, and digital compass. The second al-Biruni's method as outlined in Kitab Tahdid Nihayat al-Amakin, underwent modifications to enable Qibla direction calculations on a global scale. To assess its accuracy, a comparative analysis was conducted with our previous research, encompassing al-Biruni (the first and the third method), Ibn al- Haytham, Abu al-Wafa, and modern (spherical trigonometry) methods. The computational results of all methods, including al- Biruni's second method, demonstrated comparable levels of precision, as indicated by levels of precision as follows: Bandung is 295.146246°, Ghazna is 251.711431°, London is 118.990581°, and Sudan is 58.719484°. These findings underscore the significance of al-Biruni's contributions and the enduring relevance of his method. The successful implementation of al- Biruni's second method algorithm facilitated the creation of an autonomous Qibla-finding mobile robot capable of rotating and aligning itself with the Qibla direction. Equipped with a buzzer as an indicator and an LCD screen for real-time display of Qibla direction data, the robot exemplifies the seamless fusion of historical Islamic scientific achievements and contemporary technological advancements.

articleTitle: Design of Seaweed Dryer Using Sugeno's Fuzzy Logic Control Approach
abstract: This research aims to develop an innovative seaweed dryer with Sugeno Fuzzy Logic Control. In Indonesia, seaweed, especially Eucheuma cottonii, has high economic value, but traditional drying risks reducing its quality. This research focuses on developing an efficient and effective drying mechanism using the fuzzy logic concept. With Sugeno Fuzzy Logic Control, this system can overcome environmental uncertainties such as temperature and humidity, and adapt well. As a result, the quality and efficiency of seaweed drying are significantly improved, potentially providing benefits to the seaweed industry and expanding the understanding of fuzzy logic in industrial control.

articleTitle: Design of Proportional-Integral-Derivative Controller Using Root Locus for Human Face Tracking System with Viola Jones Method
abstract: Human face tracking system is used in various fields, including smart home, security, industrial automation, biometrics, law enforcement, entertainment and social media. The main part of this human face tracking system is face detection using camera as sensor and servo motor control as actuator. Face detection with viola jones method is implemented to get bounding box coordinates for the detected face position. The servo motor control is used to drive the servo motor so that the detection results have a bounding box midpoint reference, coordinate for pan direction is 160 and coordinate for tilt direction is 120. This paper explains the design of Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controller using root locus algorithm to determine the control action “reverse gain” to deal with negative effects of non-minimum phase systems on tracking system. From the motion of servo motor result, it can be inferred that PID controller using root locus can drive the servo motor to steady state conditions, reach the bounding box midpoint reference. It means, this system is successfully track the human face position with smaller overshoot (0.512%), faster settling time (1.087 ms) on pan direction and smaller overshoot (0.472%), faster settling time (1.030 ms) on tilt direction.

articleTitle: Communication Between Control Modules on the Mouse for the Disabled
abstract: Disabled people have difficulty operating a standard mouse on a table. Therefore, in previous studies, mouse for people with disabilities began to be developed. A disabled mouse consists of a hardware part and a software part. The software part is in charge of converting arm movements into mouse cursor movements on the monitor screen. While the hardware section discussed in this article includes control hardware in the arms and control hardware in the legs. The discussion in this article covers communication between the two control modules that use Wifi. The data sent to the computer from both modules include inertial sensor data and data from all five footswitches. The test results show that the inertial sensor and footswitch data can be sent correctly to the computer, with a 100% success rate in data transmission from the module Arm and module Foot to the PC application.

articleTitle: Forecasting System of Wind Speed and Direction by Neural Network
abstract: This paper discusses the neural network that is used to forecast wind speed and direction by combining methods of three-dimensional convolutional neural networks (3D-CNN), convolutional long short-term memory (CLSTM), and two-dimensional CNN (2D-CNN). Its method is called 3CN-CLSTM-2CN. Combining the three methods is to diminish the forecasted error and training time compared to the 3CN-CLSTM method. The input of the forecast system is the wind vector in the form of image data that indicates the image of time-sequential which is given by the Automated Meteorological Data Acquisition System (AMeDAS), Japan. Evaluate the forecast system used by the root mean square error (RMSE) between observed data and forecast data. For verification, the usefulness of the proposed forecasted system is compared with the persistent system. The suggested forecasting system's objective is to increase prediction accuracy for each season, which is typical of Japan. The proposed forecasted system by 3CN-CLSTM-2CN for each season in one-year data can increase around 16.11-26.47% to wind speed and around 20.69-23.34% to wind direction over the persistent system, which has a greater accuracy than the 3CN-CLSTM system. So, it was suitable that the 3CN-CLSTM-2CN system be the most robust forecasting system.

articleTitle: Implementation of Deep Learning With Resnet50 Modification for Clove classification
abstract: The ISO 2254-2004 standard divides cloves into three categories: whole, headless, and mother clove. Whole and headless cloves are usually processed in various products such as medicines, flavorings, and cosmetics. In contrast, mother clove is prepared for clove nurseries; even so, the employees of the clove owners are doing the clove harvest, the mother clove type is still being harvested. This is because when gathering, there are still employees of the clove owner who cannot tell the difference between headless and mother cloves. In the end, when sold, the buyer reduces the price. So, it is necessary to introduce clove types early to protect farmers. The initial identification process for this type of clove utilizes digital image processing using the Resnet50 deep learning method. In this study, we not only apply Resnet50 but also modify the Resnet50 architecture so that the method's performance in clove-type classification can be improved. The research results prove that changing Resnet50 by adding three layers can increase system accuracy by 9% in classifying clove types into three parts.

articleTitle: Performance of Optimization Techniques in the Deep Learning Approach for Classification of Covid-19 Pneumonia
abstract: This study concerns the COVID-19 pneumonia classification based on X-ray images of the lungs using a deep learning-based approach. One of the crucial parts of the deep learning approach is the optimization process. Thus, determining the optimization technique precisely is crucial to producing optimal performance from the deep learning approach. The problem is that there is no single optimization technique that produces the best performance in all cases. In this study, various optimization techniques are tested to evaluate their effectiveness in the classification of covid-19 pneumonia. The approach in the study uses the CNN method. Three categories are used to carry out the classification, namely covid19 pneumonia (inflamed lungs due to covid-19), pneumonia (inflamed lungs due to factors other than Covid-19), and normal (healthy lungs). The optimization techniques tested included RMSprop, Adadelta, Adam, Adamax, and Nadam. In the experimental process, we test the method on a lung image dataset consisting of 3,900 training images, 450 validation images, and 225 test images. The result of this study concludes that the performance of the Adamax technique outperforms other optimization techniques. The evaluation of the Adamax technique result in accuracy, precision, recall, and f1 score of 95.11%, 0.9596, 0.9511, and 0.9553, respectively.

articleTitle: Optimization and Development of Raspberry Pi 4 Model B for the Internet of Things
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) in this manuscript is how to utilize the Raspberry Pi 4 Model B, which has reliable specifications in becoming a mini-PC function; as a mini processor that has powerful capabilities, the Raspberry Pi 4 model B was developed from previous versions, such as power supply models and graphics or monitor ports with mini HDMI ports and also on the development side of the Python 3 programming language. Raspberry Pi can also be developed with Radio Frequency devices such as ZigBee and LoRa modules. Raspberry Pi 4 B can also be IoT sources that can provide specific and real-time information, for example, CPU temperature information when the Raspberry Pi 4 is operating. Cloud servers or application servers such as The Things Network or Thingspeak MatLab are used as real-time data information in graphs or images that can be viewed on various platforms utilizing a Web desktop or Mobile with an internet connection. From the analysis results, the Raspberry Pi 4 CPU has a temperature range of 40-55 degrees Celsius.

articleTitle: Prediction of Whiteleg Shrimp Feed Requirement Using k-Nearest Neighbours Regression
abstract: Some Whiteleg shrimp farms had minimum facilities for collecting data, so they had a limited amount of data variance. This research aimed to predict Whiteleg shrimp feed requirements with limited variations and the amount of available data to get a minimum error rate. Because the available data is only 69 daily feed consumption data, the knearest Neighbours (kNN) Regression method is suitable to predict the following feed requirements target. The raw data was divided into 50 training data and 19 test data. The raw data will be converted into 2-dimensional data with columns indicating the number of features. Several experiments were carried out by changing the number of features and value of knearest neighbors. Overall, the MAPE range obtained was in a good or highly accurate category, which is 6.11% - 14.52%. The best MAPE (6.11%) was achieved when the number of features and the k value were two.

articleTitle: Distance-Based Fuzzy MCDM Methods for a Supplier Selection Decision-Making Model
abstract: Making the decision to select the best suppliers is a critical process within a company as it impacts all aspects from upstream to downstream. However, this decision-making process is often challenging due to the involvement of multiple factors and suppliers. Multiple criteria decision-making (MCDM) methods are commonly proposed to address this issue. In this study, two MCDM methods, namely fuzzy technique for order of preference by similarity to ideal solution (FTOPSIS) and fuzzy evaluation based on distance from average solution (FEDAS), were chosen to select suppliers and were tested on a small-scale retail company in Indonesia. These two methods are categorized as distance-based MCDM methods that have been widely applied due to their practical capabilities. In this decision-making model, five criteria have been identified: service (C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>), delivery (C2), quality of product (C3), price of product (C4), and production capacity (C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>), involving three suppliers. By using the best-worst method (BWM), the most important criterion was C4, with a weight of 0.503. The comparison results of both methods recommended Supplier A as the best supplier. FTOPSIS and FEDAS indicate significant performance scores for the best supplier of 0.783 and 0.837, respectively. Notably, both methods produced relatively similar and stable results. This demonstrates the reliability of both methods for use in this case. Nonetheless, future studies need to be extended to involve a larger system scale and sensitivity analysis to make the decision-making model more comprehensive.

articleTitle: Digital Marketplace Design & Development for Creative Recycle Product
abstract: The increasing issue of recycling and the lack of consideration for the end-of-life treatment of synthetic polymers have led to significant environmental and health concerns. Encouraging pro-environmental behaviors, such as recycling, is crucial to address this issue. Leveraging the widespread use of the internet. This research project proposed to make a web based marketplace application to open business opportunities for waste craftsmen, by showcasing and selling their work through a dedicated marketplace. This project aligns with previous research highlighting the effectiveness of web- based applications in increasing recycling behaviors and awareness. This research aims to reduce waste accumulation in Indonesia while increasing the value and appreciation of recycled materials as art pieces or practical tools, also by helping economic growth for every craftsmen that place their product in out website. In conclusion, this research contributes to the efforts of promoting recycling, raising awareness about waste management, and supporting waste craftsmen.

articleTitle: Soft Set Based Clustering and Its Comparison on Categorical Data
abstract: Categorical data clustering is problematic since it is difficult or complex to determine how comparable the data is. Several methods, most recently centroid-based strategies, have been developed to reduce the complexity of the similarity of categorical data. These methods nevertheless result in lengthy processing durations. Another method, soft set-based clustering (SSC), based on the probability function of multivariate multinomial distributions, is suggested in this article. Soft sets are used to represent the data, and each soft set has a probability for each object. The joint cluster distribution function determines the probability for each object after the multivariate multinomial distribution function. The connected cluster would receive the highest likelihood. Benchmark data sets from UCI machine learning are used to compare the performance of the approach to the baseline techniques. The outcomes demonstrate that the suggested strategy performed better in purity, rank index, and calculation time.

articleTitle: Autism Screening Prediction Based on Multi-kernel Support Vector Machine
abstract: Autism is a group neurodevelopmental disorder that affects a person's ability to communicate, engage with others, and act in specific ways. Screening and early prediction of autism are important in supporting the proper diagnosis and effective early intervention. However, early detection of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) can be challenging since it is behavior-based and more complicated to identify biologically. Our classification system uses ten questions from the Autism-Spectrum Quotient (AQ) Test and four specific subject data features. Support Vector Machine (SVM) is a machine learning method that has shown effectiveness in prediction and classification. However, when the investigation data has complex non-linear characteristics, SVM with a single kernel may not perform as well. Our study proposed a multi-kernel SVM method to improve the model's accuracy. The classification evaluation parameters, including accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score, were applied to evaluate the prediction model's effectiveness. Our experiment results indicate that the Multi-kernel SVM approach has a robust performance in predicting autism. Furthermore, our proposed method's performance is outstanding, with an accuracy of 0.976; the normal class can be distinguished with high precision, recall, and f1-score, whereas the ASD class has an ideal precision of 1.00.

articleTitle: Performance of LoRaWAN in Multi-Node
abstract: This research reviews the Performance of LoRaWAN using RF96 and simulation OMNeT++. RF96 is one of the chips used for LoRaWAncommunication; as a whole, LoRa Communication is formed from Radio Frequency communication between LoRa end-nodes and TCP/IP on the programming side of the Gateway and Application Server. This article explicitly discusses RF communication systems with many nodes or multi-nodes. This research uses OMNET++ simulation, which integrates and equalizes all components of RF96, starting from Bit-rate ability, SF, Bandwidth, CR, and other details integrated into one OMNET++ parameter. The parameters that can be calculated are RSSI, SNR, Bit-Rate Error Rate, Packet Loss, etc. This system, in detail, compares the number of end nodes communicated. The development of the results of this analysis is more of an approach to the Internet of Things; moreover, in this research, tests were conducted with 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 50, 75, and 100 Nodes of LoRa, and analyzed in detail the output of parameters and Quality of Services from LoRaWancommunication.

articleTitle: Process Mining Approach to Analyze Engagement in Campaign Activities
abstract: Campaign strategies are evolving because of developments in communication technologies. Campaign activities have become more attractive to the younger generation with the existence of social media. There is much research related to campaigns, but it focuses on data collection and content. This research tries to look at it from the other side, namely from the perspective of the campaign team. How can teams improve performance and ensure that strategies are executed correctly? The analysis was carried out using process mining. The methodology used is the Project Mining Methodology, supported by data, identification, conformity checking, and quality improvement. The data used was taken from a Facebook group that was specifically created and operated during the 100 days of the official campaign. Interactions occurred with 2215 members with 975 active members, of which there were 357 posts, 8755 reactions, 1275 comments, and 280 shares. The results obtained from this process show weekly posting patterns and responses. Furthermore, we can see the involvement of key figures in the activities of the campaign group.

articleTitle: Implementation Frequent Pattern Growth (FP-Growth) Algorithm on Market Basket Analysis for Determining Consumer Purchasing Patterns (Case Study: XYZ Coffee Shop)
abstract: Globally, the food and beverage industry continues to experience rapid expansion in multiple regions. In following the COVID-19 pandemic, the food and beverage industry has experienced a gradual but consistent expansion. In Indonesia, the food and beverage industry is a thriving economic sector, driven by the country's expanding population and the commensurate rise in demand for food and beverages. Coffee shops are one of the segments of the food and beverage industry. In determining consumer interest in buying coffee drinks, promotional strategies are used to attract customers who are initially not interested in making purchases, thereby increasing the customer's desire to get and or be interested in the product. FP-Growth is a data mining technique that identifies frequently occurring items without requiring candidate production. The results obtained products with a minimum support value of 50%; if a customer buys Pentol 8K, then the customer will also buy KS Hazelnut with a support value of 58.5%. In the interim, the confidence value is 85.7%. The rules are attained with a minimum support value of 50% and a minimum confidence of 80% if KS Hazelnut and Pentol 8K are purchased. Thus, when consumers buy KS Hazelnut, they will buy Pentol 8K food, used as a sales marketing parameter and promotional material.

articleTitle: Detecting Fine-Grained Emotions from COVID-19 Tweets Using Transformer-Based Architecture
abstract: With the proliferation of social media, the task of identifying emotions in textual content has become increasingly relevant. Automating the task of detecting emotions from social media content has a wide range of applications today. In this work, we investigate the efficacy of pre-trained transformer models to detect fine-grained emotions from real-world tweets. We conduct experiments to fine-tune the DistilBERT and XLNet transformers to recognize nine emotions including neutral, anger, anticipation, disgust, fear, joy, sadness, surprise and trust. Our DistilBERT and XLNet based models exhibit an F1-score of 0.6429 and 0.6679 respectively. The results are promising when compared with similar transformer-based models for fine-grained emotion recognition. We conclude from our study that fine-grained emotion detection from microblogs using transformers although promising is also challenging. The challenge is primarily on account of two reasons: a) difficulty in differentiating between intrinsically similar emotions and b) difficulty in building a large and balanced annotated corpus from real-world tweets.

articleTitle: iTCLab PID Control Tuning Using Deep Learning
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach for tuning Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controllers using deep learning techniques, specifically applied to the iTCLab, an advanced industrial control laboratory system. PID controllers are widely used in industrial processes for their simplicity and effectiveness. However, their performance heavily relies on proper tuning, which can be a complex and time-consuming task. In this study, we leverage the capabilities of deep learning to automate and optimize the PID tuning process for the iTCLab setup. We propose a data-driven methodology that combines system identification, Deep Learning networks, and optimization algorithms to achieve superior PID controller tuning.

articleTitle: Enhancing Voice Security through Rikitake Chaosbased Encryption System
abstract: With the increasing reliance on voice communication and the growing need for secure information transmission, cryptography has become vital in enhancing communication security. Chaos-based cryptography has emerged as an innovative approach to strengthen existing cryptographic techniques. In this study, we propose the utilization of the Rikitake chaotic system as an alternative method for voice encryption. Our research involves a comprehensive analysis of the Rikitake chaos system, including phase diagram analysis, time series analysis, Lyapunov exponents, and Poincaré maps. Additionally, we conducted various analyses specifically focused on voice encryption, such as voice signal plots comprising waveforms, Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), spectrograms, correlation coefficients, entropy analysis, and Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE). The voice correlation analysis showed average values of -0.00253 for Original-Encrypted and 0.9985 for Original-Decrypted. Additionally, entropy analysis resulted in averages of 7.999097667 for Original-Encrypted and 0.22433 for OriginalDecrypted. For density variations of 0.10 and 0.01, the RMSE analysis produced average results of 0.1001 and 0.0101, respectively. The research findings strongly suggest that the Rikitake chaotic system holds promise for voice signal encryption, showcasing its potential effectiveness in enhancing communication security. These findings contribute to a better understanding of the use of chaotic systems in voice encryption and illustrate the potential effectiveness in securing voice communication. Thus, the Rikitake chaotic system can make a significant contribution to the development of cryptographic technology for protecting sensitive voice information.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable of Palm Tree Vivaldi Antenna Using Square Ring Resonator for Cognitive Radio Applications
abstract: Cognitive radio is an innovation of ICT infrastructure to support antenna operation in Bluetooth, WLAN, and WiMax communications applications. This letter presents a developed palm tree Vivaldi antenna with dimensions of 250 × 250 mm that can operate at a frequency of 0.6–3.4 GHz. The reconfigurable technique is the SRR (Split Ring Resonator), which creates a gap in the antenna design. The SRR form in this letter is DSSR (Double Square Split Resonance) combined with the switching technique using diodes. There are four DSSR placed in the area of the spread path of the electromagnetic field at the tapper slot line. The diode switching technique provides two conditions on or off and diodes attached to the DSSR input. In this letter, there are four modes of diodes that produce frequency changes. The results simulation antennas can operate at 0.5-0.7 GHz, 1.6-2.0 GHz, 2.3-2.6 GHz, 2.5-3.1 GHz, 2.5-3.2 GHz, 3.3-3.4 GHz. The resulting return loss has a notch band area that reduces communication system interference when applied to cognitive radio in the area of WLAN, WiFI, and Bluetooth.

articleTitle: Game Technology Approach for Biology Education (Immune System) Delivery at Elementary Level
abstract: In recent years there have been many attempts to gamify our education system. Especially regarding the complexity and the unknown aspects of the human body. The study of the immune system is one of the most difficult and advanced lessons for an elementary to high school student. This is why we want to create a way to gamify the process of learning with this paper. This paper presents an approach in game technology to deliver biology education to the immune system. The paper focuses on a literature and theoretical review of game technologies and their approach to education. The proposed approach includes the design and development of an interactive platforming game with a game-based learning environment that allows students to interact and participate in their learning. The findings and insights from this research contribute to the field of biology education by demonstrating the effectiveness and viability of game technology approaches for teaching complex scientific concepts, such as the immune system, to elementary and junior high school students. Lastly, this paper contributes to improving a learner's education and ability in biology through unique interactive, and interesting games.

articleTitle: Development of Grid Connected Solar PV Power Management Controller with Internet of Things-Based Real Time Data Checking
abstract: The power supply is the de-facto standard of any electrical and electronic appliances that require operation and control, and it is all dependent on it. Batteries have been extensively used for many years and decades as a leading source of energy storage for diversified electrical and electronics systems such as electric vehicles, electronics systems and devices, communication systems, electric trains and ships, power systems, and most notably renewable energy systems. Nonetheless, when the energy storage is wearied out, the external AC power source is essential. In recent years, external energy dilemmas and increasing environmental concerns have pushed stakeholders and policy makers to invest in renewable energy systems, such as solar PV systems. Further, the advent of the Internet of Things achieved great attention from developers, programmers, and engineers in recent years. In this work, the development and design of grid-tied solar PV power management controller with IoT–based real-time data checking is presented. The whole prototype model is portrayed by the battery energy storage connected to the source utility AC power line through the AC/DC converter, and a solar photovoltaic panel buttoned with a DC/DC power converter. The intelligent energy management system for the overall prototype operation, administered by the ESP32 microcontroller, and the Internet of Things platform was used for the real-time health condition monitoring with the aid of the Android-based mobile phone. The experimental results reveal that the prototype and system model are compelling.

articleTitle: Clustering Coping Capacity Using HCSS
abstract: Coping capacity, or the capability of individuals, communities, and societies to successfully respond to and recover from bad events, is a critical component of disaster risk reduction. Formulating successful disaster preparedness, response, and recovery plans requires understanding coping capacity. Building resilient communities that can face landslide difficulties and lowering susceptibility needs assessing and improving landslide coping capacity. Clustering based on the soft set method is used in this study to identify separate groups of communities with comparable coping ability features and to enable focused interventions and resource allocation. The experiment provides 3 clusters based on the Dunn Index value. The disaster risk knowledge score of C1 and C2 are obtained at 3 on average, while C2 is obtained at 1.67. The mitigation knowledge scores for C1,c2 and C2 are obtained 1.67, 3 and 2, respectively. Investigators or the government can use this to provide recommendations to determine different treatments and create sensible regulations to promote catastrophe risk reduction and neighbourhood safety in the area.

articleTitle: Enhancing Thematic Holy Quran Verse Retrieval through Vector Space Model and Query Expansion for Effective Query Answering
abstract: The Quran provides valuable insights into various aspects of life, including information about the natural world, such as animals and plants. Developing an information retrieval system can greatly facilitate the search for specific content within the Quran. This system utilizes a cosine similarity approach and query expansion techniques to rank and expand the retrieved documents according to the user's needs. In this research, the Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) weighting method is employed, following preprocessing steps for both the documents and queries. The primary objectives of this study are to assess accuracy, precision, and recall values. Notably, the inclusion of query expansion has led to an improved recall value compared to previous research, resulting in a 99.32% accuracy rate, a 5.83% increase in precision (from 83.93%), and a system's ability to capture 8.75% of the relevant verse (compared to the previous 93.51%). This signifies that all verses can be invoked, displayed, or expanded, providing a more comprehensive query experience.

articleTitle: Design of Formalin Detection System in Food Based on Artificial Neural Network
abstract: Most snacks and food today use a lot of preservatives so that they last longer and don't spoil quickly. The most commonly used preservative is formalin. Formalin is a toxic chemical that is often used as a preservative for biological samples such as preserving corpses. The existence of formalin is difficult to detect by the five human senses. Testing for formalin is usually carried out in a laboratory, so it is not easy for the public to do it. Therefore, this study proposes to design a tool to detect formalin based on a microcontroller. This tool is very important because it contributes to being able to test food with formalin practically, effectively, and quickly. It uses an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) method and it uses a gas sensor type HCHO WSP2110 and type MQ-138 to detect steam produced from heating. The results showed that The MQ-138 sensor is more sensitive to formalin than the HCHO WSP2110. The percentage of success of the tool in detecting the presence of formalin in food was 86.67%.

articleTitle: Comparison 5 Level Cascade H-bridge Multilevel Inverter Circuit with LC Filter and Without LC Filter
abstract: The 5-level Cascade H-bridge multilevel inverter has become an attractive choice in industrial applications and renewable power systems. The output wave quality produced by this multilevel inverter has an important role in ensuring optimal performance of the system. In this study, a performance comparison analysis was carried out between a 5-level Cascade H-bridge multilevel inverter with the use of an LC filter after the inverter and a configuration without an LC filter. The simulation results show that the use of an LC filter after the inverter produces a purer output signal by reducing unwanted harmonic components. The inverter without LC filter has a THD of 28.99%, while with an LC filter the THD is 8%. The use of LC filters improves the quality of the output signal and the performance of a 5-level multilevel inverter.

articleTitle: Hybridization of Particle Swarm Optimization and Variable Neighborhood Search for Multi-Site Aggregates Production Planning in the Home Textile Industry
abstract: Aggregate production planning is an essential stage in the production process by companies because the planning stage will affect the next stage. It will be crucial if the company has several production branch locations or can be referred to as multi-site. The rules that apply and the parameter values for each production branch will undoubtedly be different from other production branches. This raises problems for the company in addition to uncertain consumer demand problems. This problem is quite complicated and very important to solve. The author resolves the problems faced by the company by applying the proposed method, namely the hybridization of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Variable Neighborhood Search (VNS). The solution generated by the proposed method proved optimum.

articleTitle: Sperm Classification of X and Y Chromosomes Based on Lazy Learning Using K-NN
abstract: Sperm cells can be differentiated into 2 based on their sex chromosomes. Sperm cells for male have Y chromosome, while sperm cells for female have an X chromosome. To distinguish between X and Y chromosomes can be seen from the head size of the sperm cell which is X chromosome sperm cells have a larger head size than Y chromosome sperm cells. Therefore, the lazy learning method is used in the k-nearest neighbor algorithm to classify X chromosome sperm cells and Y chromosome sperm cells. So, feature extraction process is needed to obtain the characteristics of the sperm object that can distinguish X chromosome sperm cells and Y chromosome sperm cells. The features are length and width of sperm head in form of an image to determine the head size in each sperm data.

articleTitle: Normalized Traffic Features Using Graph Signal Processing for Traffic Flow Prediction
abstract: Traffic forecasting is essential for the intelligent transportation system and is applied to managing traffic networks. Recently, there has been a growing interest in incorporating spatial and temporal variables into the methodology of traffic forecasting. The primary emphasis of modern research lies in the complex architecture of graph neural networks. In contrast, preprocessing data for the input is also essential. Especially traffic data, such as traffic flows, have high nonlinearity and complex patterns. The traffic graph signal is attributes that are associated with the nodes. In this paper, the step of preprocessing data utilized graph signal processing (GSP) to filter noise from traffic signal data before the traffic flow data was applied for prediction tasks. The adjusted parameter for filtering noise was used. In this paper, the parameter was set from 0.1 to 10. The result shows that the increasing parameter filter of the graph data was smoothed filtered. Moreover, the smooth data is affected by the time horizons. For the increasing time horizon, we can use the large parameter and get the prediction error smaller than the shorter time horizon.

articleTitle: CFD Simulation of the Effect of Adding a Sludge Zone to the Sequencing Batch Reactor for Fluid Turbulence
abstract: The Sequencing Batch Reactor (SBR) flow turbulence analysis aims to increase the dissolved oxygen (DO) in wastewater. This DO is a significant factor that influences the abundance of microbes in SBR. These microbes act as wastewater pollutants degraders in the SBR. The other problem of SBR, the sludge is frequently included in the effluent, reducing the quality of the treated wastewater. As a result, the aim of this study is to examine the effects of turbulence in square-cylindrical SBRs, as well as the effects of adding a sludge zone at the bottom of the SBR. This research is divided into two activities, turbulence analysis using Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD), and laboratory scale design of an SBR prototype complete with impeller. On a laboratory scale, the variables used are hydraulic retention time and impeller rotation speed of 50 and 150 rpm. The experiment results showed that a rectangular-shaped SBR with a sludge zone could achieve an optimal DO of 4.04 mg/L. CFD modelling resulted in similar results; flow turbulence was evenly distributed throughout the reactor, increasing the DO content.

articleTitle: Design and Build a Passenger Prediction Information System Using Gated Recurrent Unit Deep Learning Algorithm
abstract: Sumenep is a district located in the eastern part of the island of Madura. Sumenep Regency has many islands that are still within its scope. Sea transportation is an essential means of traveling to Sapudi Island. Therefore, the increase in passengers needs to be considered in sailing safety. To make the prediction process for the number of sea transportation passengers, the Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) method is used as a method in deep learning that is capable of making predictions. The data obtained is passenger data for the years 2020 - 2023 with a seasonal data type. The suitable parameters during the GRU method testing were the number of neurons, epochs, and learning rates of 64,200 and 0.1 with a MAPE error of 9.93. With an error value <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ < 10 \%$</tex>, then GRU can be ascertained as an excellent method for predicting the amount of sea transportation passenger data in Sumenep towards Sapudi Island. To carry out the prediction process, the application is based on WEB so that all users can use and find out the results of passenger predictions using the GRU method.

articleTitle: High Gain and Broadband mmWave Vivaldi Antenna for 5G High Band Application
abstract: This work presents the performance of a Vivaldi antenna for the 5G high band spectrum covering 24.25 – 27.5 GHz. The Vivaldi antennas are known widely for their wideband bandwidth and high gain due to their tapered slot design. We have optimized the proposed Vivaldi antenna through four development steps, including applying the gradual corrugated edges, and circular slots, adding a conductive triangle, and using a shorting pin. Based on the simulated results, the proposed Vivaldi antenna has an impedance bandwidth (IBW) of around 7.1 GHz, covering 22.1 GHz to 29.2 GHz. Next, the simulated VSWR values are in the range of 1.09 to 1.48 at 24.25 – 27.5 GHz. Furthermore, the proposed Vivaldi antenna produces a gain in the range of 6.2 to 9.4 dBi, with a peak gain at a frequency of 27.4 GHz and an angular width (3 dB) is 42°. The proposed Vivaldi exhibits good characteristics for the millimeter wave spectrum.

articleTitle: Air Temperature Forecasting Based on Stacking Machine Learning Model with Multi-Step Time Series
abstract: Forecasting air temperature is very influential in various areas of fields. Temperature is an fundamental factor that influences weather. Changes in the temperature in that environment can mark changes in environmental weather. Forecasting the inside temperature and long waiting time determines the planning environment and planning of electrical energy resources. The purpose of this study is to forecast air temperature from the data recorded by the temperature sensor. Therefore, in this work, we propose that temperature forecasting is based on an ensemble of numerous machine learning models to obtain the best model accuracy. We have used the stacking ensemble model to forecast air temperature. A combination of models to find the best model is needed to build a predictive model. Using the base layer model and the number of base classifier models significantly affects the model prediction error. The best ensemble model accomplished is the combination model (Gradient Boosting Regression-Support Vector Regression) - Gradient Boosting Regression meta-model with a MAPE value of 0.0096.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: SkinMate: Mobile-Based Application for Detecting Multi-Class Skin Diseases Classification Using Pre-Trained MobileNetV2 on CNN Architecture
abstract: The skin has a very significant role in humans. But unfortunately, the skin is one of the organs vulnerable to disease. Skin diseases can have an impact on the annoying itching, pain, emotional, and social feelings of the sufferer. The causes of skin diseases include bacteria, fungi, viruses, dust, and allergies. Delay in treatment can exacerbate the condition of the affected skin. Therefore, the research proposed a skin disease detection mobile application for early diagnosis. The total of skin disease images is 2.747 data, which is divided into five classes and separated into training and validation data. The category of the dataset includes Acne Vulgaris, Actinic Keratosis, Nail Fungus, Psoriasis, and Seborrheic Keratoses. The development of this application uses several augmentation techniques so that the model gets input training data from various image forms, and then uses pre-trained MobileNetV2, which has low latency and low power as needed on mobile devices. The development of this application also uses the TensorFlow Lite model for inference with ML Kit on Android. The model performance gave the best accuracy of 90.62%, precision of 89%, recall of 90%, and F1- score of 89%. These results indicate that the classifying of skin diseases using the pre-trained MobileNetV2 on CNN architecture is feasible.

articleTitle: Implementation of Support Vector Machine Method to Predict Harvest Readiness of Wonosalam Coffee Fruits
abstract: The quality of coffee is primarily determined by the maturity level of the fruit at harvest time. If the coffee fruit is picked too early, the quality and flavor will not reach its full potential. On the other hand, if the coffee fruit is overripe, it can affect the acidity and taste of the coffee produced. The first stage is picking coffee cherries from the tree by Wonosalam coffee farmers. The picking is done by selecting ripe coffee cherries because if immature cherries are mixed in, the quality and flavor of the coffee may be affected. In addition to the maturity level, fruit defects also affect the quality. Nowadays, picking is done manually by farmers. Farmers often pick unripe fruit in a hurry, resulting in the harvesting of unripe and deformed fruit. As a result, farmers have to re-sort, which reduces their productivity. Therefore, an image processing-based Wonosalam coffee fruit quality detection tool is proposed. This research uses one of the image processing methods used in classifying the maturity of coffee fruit that is ready to harvest, namely the Support Vector Machine (SVM) method. The results showed that the SVM method in classifying the readiness of coffee fruit harvest obtained a total accuracy of 85%.

articleTitle: Solar Tracking System Dual Axis using Proportional Integral Derivative (PID) Controller
abstract: The potential for renewable energy in Indonesia is very high, including solar energy. Photovoltaic systems convert sunlight into electricity, where the result depends on the type of solar panel, the solar irradiance of the area, the geographical location and other factors. One of the efforts to increase the capture of solar radiation is solar tracking systems, where the way it works is the solar panel detects and follows the direction of the highest intensity of sunlight to obtain maximum power. The movement of the motor when tracking is not smooth, causing the solar tracking system not to get the highest light intensity needed to charge the battery. Therefore, in this study, the linear movement of the actuator was controlled using the Proportional Integral Derivative (PID) method so that the movement was smooth. Based on the test results, the solar tracking system with the PID method can provide stable control. This is proven by the error resulting from the lux sensor reading on the X-axis of 0.3 and the Y-axis of 0.2, which means it is accurate. Then the gain of voltage, power and current is also greater than without using the PID method.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Programmable Single Ended Primary Inductor Converter Using Proportional Integral Derivative Method
abstract: At this time, the use of DC (Direct Current) power supplies is very important for the industrial and educational world. Almost all electronic components use DC power supplies. Due to the use of this diverse DC power supply, a system is needed that is able to convert DC voltage from one quantity to another. DC-DC converter is a device that provides direct DC power generated through the conversion of input DC voltage into a lower or higher output DC voltage. In this study, a Programmable Single Ended Primary Inductor Converter using the PID (Proportional Integral Derivative) method is designed and implemented to make a DC to DC converter that has a fixed and stable output voltage even though the input voltage changes. The level of stability of the output voltage is based on the output voltage and current detected by the sensor then those sensor data are processed by the STM32F103C8T6 microcontroller. Then the microcontroller will determine the duty cycle to control the switching circuit and the output voltage will match the predetermined setpoint. This circuit can work at a maximum load of up to 10A. PID testing produces an output voltage that takes 1.88ms to reach the setpoint voltage with a Kp value of 0.08537, a Ki value of 5.33695, and a Kd value of 0.05143. The lowest efficiency is 83.21 % and the highest one is 99.86%.

articleTitle: Beef Image Classification Using the Inception V3 Transfer Learning Model
abstract: Economic conditions and increased incomes can impact rising prices for beef and other consumer products. The increase in consumption needs in the community causes the high cost of beef in the market. The high cost of meat is often taken advantage of by irresponsible people by selling beef that is not fresh or mixing fresh and not-fresh meat. The level of freshness of the beef itself can be seen manually by looking directly at the color and texture of the beef. However, not all people can distinguish which meat is fresh and which is not. A model that can classify beef automatically is needed. This research will use machine learning to predict fresh, half-fresh, and spoiled meat images. The machine learning model will use the Inception V3 transfer learning architecture model. The research contribution is using additional datasets to produce different results and obtain the beef image classification model. The results of the model performance evaluation show an accuracy value of 87.14%, a precision of 87.14%, a recall of 87.14%, and an f1 score of 88.28%. These results indicate that the Inception V3 architectural model is the best fit for use in beef classification. The information obtained from the experiments shows that the model evaluation results using Inception are more optimal than the Xception evaluation results from earlier research.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence-Based System ‘SiMoniK’ for MSMEs
abstract: Artificial intelligence was recently implemented in various fields. One of these applied artificial intelligence systems was the Performance Monitoring System “SiMoniK” for MSMEs. This system was designed through the C4.5 algorithm and the Porat-Rank method. The C4.5 algorithm was applied to classify the MSMEs into three classifications, e.g. the micro enterprise classification, the small enterprise classification, and the medium enterprise classification. Moreover, the Porat-Rank method was also applied to distribute the solving-problem recommendations and to improve the independence of MSMEs. The result of this study was that the C4.5 algorithm could classify the MSME data correctly in the form of an accuracy value of 99.2%. Besides, the Porat-Rank method could also provide recommendations in the form of outstanding quality with an NDCG mean value of 0.87.

articleTitle: Web Scraping for Summarization of Freelance Job Website Using Vector Space Model
abstract: In the contemporary digital age, the internet plays a central role in various community activities, much like it does in the realm of work. Nowadays, numerous platforms offer job listings, particularly geared toward freelancers. To access this information, users typically have to visit multiple websites to find relevant job opportunities. Web scraping presents a solution to address this challenge. Building upon prior research, we will utilize the BeautifulSoup and Selenium libraries for data collection. Our data retrieval will rely on the vector space model method to assess the similarity between the user's query and the documents. In our data examination, we achieve a perfect recall rate of 100%, but the average precision rate is at 56%. This is explained by the fact that our data search uses three factors, increasing the possibility that when a document contains a word from the user's query, even if it doesn't exactly fit the context, unrelated material will be retrieved. We can show the outcomes of data processing and walk people through the site scraping, data processing, and data retrieval processes by utilizing the Python Streamlit framework. This study's main objective is to use web scraping techniques to get information from freelancing websites. Users may get data from various websites by using the vector space model technique, eliminating the need to visit each freelancing site separately. Furthermore, by employing data visualization in a web application developed with the Streamlit framework, we can present the web scraping results in a more user-friendly format, ultimately saving users valuable time.

articleTitle: E-Marketplace Selection for Indonesian MSMEs: A Sentiment Analysis Approach Combining Lexicon-Based and Support Vector Machine
abstract: This study aims to examine e-marketplace performance using Lexicon-based research method and Support Vector Machine based on sentiment analysis to help Micro, Small, and Medium enterprises with the best-fit recommendation. Six popular e-marketplaces in Indonesia, including Tiktokshop, Shopee, Lazada, Tokopedia, Bukalapak, and Blibli.com, were selected as case studies. The findings show that Lazada and Tiktokshop gained the highest positive review value, totaling 96.04% with an accuracy rate of 93%, followed by Tiktokshop with 92% accuracy. Tokopedia ranked third with a review value of 95.47% and an accuracy value of 91%, while Blibli.com attained a total of 94.56% with 95% accuracy. Shopee secured value of 91.46% with 90% accuracy, and Bukalapak concluded with 90.92% and 89% accuracy. This research provides two significant contributions. First, it makes a scientific contribution by employing a combined lexicon-based and SVM model for sentiment analysis of e-marketplaces in Indonesia. Second, while this study is in the Indonesian context, the approach and findings offer a practical contribution for Micro, Small, and Medium enterprises owners selecting suitable e-marketplaces for their marketing strategies.

articleTitle: Detect Areas of Upward and Downward Fluctuations in Bitcoin Prices Using Patterned Datasets
abstract: Many researchers have proposed various theories and techniques to estimate the value of Bitcoin. However, there is still a great opportunity to suggest a new approach to Bitcoin forecasting. This research will examine the concept of forming a patterned dataset to prove the hypothesis regarding the start of a bitcoin price fluctuation until the end of the fluctuation using patterned dataset pairs in conditions of price decline (moon) and in conditions of price decline (crash). Patterned datasets were initially built from data on the movement of all cryptocurrency assets on a digital cryptocurrency trading market. The Patterned Dataset is programmed based on the response of all crypto assets to changes in the price of bitcoin over time. Patterned datasets are better able to describe the conditions of the digital cryptocurrency market, along with patterns of potential increases and decreases in Bitcoin prices in particular and cryptocurrencies in general. To deepen the observations, resampling of the patterned dataset was carried out with a 4-hour timeframe using the mean, median, min, max, and sum filter functions on pairs of crash and moon conditions per month. The results show that filter functions other than sum, namely mean, median, min, and max, provide markings of fluctuation area patterns that are easier to recognize. Two hypotheses related to fluctuations were also successfully proven in this research.

articleTitle: Mobile Robot Equipped with Thermal Camera and YoloV5 to Detect Gas Leakage Source
abstract: Gas leaks can cause sever air contamination and are potentially harm to human health and the environment. The use of mobile robot technology in areas where gas leakage often occur, can reduce the risk of harm to human workers. Mobile robots can be equipped with accurate and precise gas sensors to provide information on the position of gas sources. However, the problem in detecting the basis of a gas leak is the presence of outside airflow, which causes dispersion this, can make gas detection difficult because it causes the gas concentration to decrease at the position of the leak source. In this research, a mobile robot was developed to determine the location of the origin of gas leaks using a thermal imaging camera and the YoloV5 algorithm. YoloV5 is a deep learning algorithm based on Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to perform object detection in one step. The results of experiments show that the mobile robot is able to accurately find the location of the gas leak with a success rate of 91.25%.

articleTitle: Profanity Detector on Twitter Using Naive Bayes and Decision Tree
abstract: In modern times, profanities can be found all over the internet including social media platforms like Twitter. The study will compare the performance of Naive Bayes and Decision Tree algorithms, which are widely used in text classification tasks. The dataset for training and testing the profanity detector will consist of an extensive collection of tweets labeled as offensive or not offensive. The dataset will be preprocessed to be used to train the models of classification. The Decision Tree achieves an accuracy of 0.94, while Multinomial Naïve Bayes achieves an 0.92 accuracy.

articleTitle: Enhancing Mobile Robot Stability and Roaming Capability Using Fuzzy-PID Control Method
abstract: Mobile robot is one of the robot categories that has the function to move places. When the robot runs there are immeasurable outside interference that affects the system response. The development of a mobile robot is the implementation of changes in horizontal, incline and decline trajectories. This causes the speed of the robot to change, so we need a mechanism that can make the mobile robot maintain stability and roaming capability for the stability of the mobile robot speed, by Fuzzy-PID). PID method to set the servo based on the input from the gyro Z, it makes the mobile robot run straight without leaving its path with constant values Kp = 5, Ki = 0 and Kd = 1. Fuzzy logic used to determine the slope that the robot can traverse, while PID to adjust the motor speed. The system response reaches a steady state with a servo value of 90 °, from 8th to 13.5th seconds. Mobile robots can maintain a stable speed when crossing horizontal, incline and decline track with constant values of Kp = 1.5, Ki = 0 and Kd = 0.2. The response given by the system reaches a steady state speed value of 0.88 at 16.4 seconds.

articleTitle: Design of a Real Time Cow Smart Collar Health and Position Monitoring System
abstract: This research aimed to realize Smart Livestock Farming (SPLF). an intelligent livestock system to monitoring farm easyly. Human resources are a major factor that operate tradisional livestock farming. A hypothesis. cost-reduction from this smart livestock monitoring system is an applying smart wireless sensor network nodes. the Internet of Things (IoT). and a Node-Microcontroller Unit (Node-MCU). The cow collar is designed to get rigorous temperature using the MLX90614 sensor. heart rate using the pulse sensor. and exact location of the animal values using the uBlox Neo-6m GPS (Global Positioning System) sensor. All of this data will be processed by NodeMCU ESP8266 and give a realtime monitoring using Internet of Things (IoT). From the testing. result that the average measurement error of : the Ublox Neo-6m GPS device is 8.2848E-06. the MLX90614 temperature sensor is 0.74%. and the pulse sensor is 3.04%.

articleTitle: Light Intensity Control and Greenhouse Monitoring System for Melon Cultivation
abstract: Melon plants require a photosynthesis process ranging from 10 to 12 hours per day. Cultivating melon plants at the greenhouse of Institut Teknologi Telkom Surabaya is challenged by the fluctuating climate of Surabaya City, which can impact the received light intensity and result in a deficiency for required photosynthesis. In addition to the light intensity level, the selection of light color for specific growth phases also influences plant development. Therefore, the purpose of this paper is to create a monitoring and light intensity control system in the greenhouse based on the color spectrum of the growth phases of melon plant, to support the growth and development of melon plants. The Fuzzy Mamdani method was chosen to establish rules for the percentage of light color based on light intensity and the growth phase of melon plants. The results show that the system's outcomes using the fuzzy method achieved an accuracy of 99.92% with a margin of error of 0.08% for the blue LED, 99.74% accuracy with a margin of error of 0.26% for the red LED, and 99.95% accuracy with a margin of error of 0.05% for the white LED, in contrast the web-based monitoring system is capable of displaying light intensity data, plant growth phases, and lamp statuses.

articleTitle: Off-Grid Solar PV System with Web-Based Data Management and Sun Tracking Capability for Brgy. 649, Baseco Compound, Manila
abstract: The accessibility of electricity drives the primal consideration for the habitability of residential homes. Upon assessment of researchers in Barangay 649, Baseco Compound, Port Area, Manila, several home residents have nonelectric supply from the utility AC distributor. This paper presents the design of a non-grid-tied solar PV to the target residents in the said barangay. The project highlights sun-tracking mechanical capability with the aid of data managementvia the web cloud, which powers up the electrical LED lights, ventilations, and charging of mobile gadgets. During testing, it was found that the designed system has increased average yield efficiency up to 50%, resulting in a 3.7KW-hr higher energy yield throughout testing, the project delivered relied electric power supply with no observed power outage.

articleTitle: K-Nearest Neighbor Method Approach in Implementing Automatic Feeding Efficiency Based on the Internet of Things in Broiler Chickens
abstract: Implementation of the Internet of Things (IoT) for Automatic Broiler Chicken Feeding Efficiency Using the K-Nearest Neighbor Method is one approach that can be used to optimize the feeding system on broiler chicken farms against the background that there are still many breeders who still provide conventional feed which often consumes time-consuming and inefficient. This research aims to help chicken farmers save time and efficiency in feeding and minimize stress levels in chickens which can result in chicken death. The system can run well as proven by the sensors functioning in measuring temperature, humidity and distance. The results of testing on the application being built include temperature, humidity and distance features of 30°C, 57% and 80, respectively.

articleTitle: Bandwidth, Gain, and Lowered-Sidelobe Level Improvement of A Circularly Polarized Slotted Waveguide Antenna Array for Ka-Band Applications
abstract: This research delivers the performance of a circularly polarized slotted waveguide antenna (CP-SWA) for Ka-band applications. Slotted waveguide antennas are suitable for millimeter wave applications due to their high-power handling, high-stable performance, low transmission loss, and high gain. Furthermore, circular polarization can reduce some effects related to multipath fading, phasing issues, reflectivity, and mismatch polarization. This work applies an arraying method for increasing the performance of the proposed antenna, and it has three CP-SWAs. Based on the simulated results, the proposed antennas have a broadband bandwidth for both the IBW and ARBW, 9.4 GHz and 7.9 GHz, respectively. Next, the proposed CP-SWA antenna array achieves a peak gain of around 11−13 dBic. In addition, arraying methods also have a good impact on lowering the sidelobe level of the antenna. There is an improved sidelobe level of 6-7 dB compared to the single antenna. The proposed CP-SWA antenna array has good characteristics for millimeter-wave applications.

articleTitle: Marine Fish Species Classification Using Transfer Learning and Residual Network
abstract: Sea fish is one source of food that can be found in coastal waters. Fishermen meet market demand and deliver products to local markets. Fish species are selected using visual observation. Artificial intelligence is expected to help this process by using deep learning. The algorithm that can be used is the Convolutional neural network. Classification of fish species: Research the shape and color of fish in depth so that the machine can help distinguish the type of fish caught. This research used nine classes of marine fish for consumption, including Tongkol, tuna, Kembung, Tenggiri, Kakap, Cakalang, Salmon, Sarden, and Baronang. Each of the nine classes of fish contains 60 training images, including 45 validation images and 10 test images, so the total images used are 534. The architecture used is a custom residual layer with data augmentation. Data limitations handled by augmentation techniques include scaling, rotation, sliding, and reflection. From the results of the research trial scenarios, it can be seen that this research can classify species with an average accuracy of 99.26%, precision of 0.9926, recall of 0.9927, and F-1 score of 0.9927 with an average computational learning time using layers custom about 3 minutes.

articleTitle: Leveraging U-Net Architecture for Accurate Localization in Brain Tumor Segmentation
abstract: This study presents an approach based on deep learning to segment brain tumors in medical imaging accurately. The segmentation of brain tumors plays a crucial role in diagnosing, planning treatments, and monitoring disease progression. However, existing methods have limitations such as time-consuming procedures, inadequate accuracy, and delayed detection. The U-Net model architecture, a widely used convolutional neural network (CNN) for medical image segmentation tasks, was employed to segment brain tumors in CT and MRI scans to overcome these challenges. The performance of the U-Net model was evaluated on datasets consisting of 32, 64, and 128 slices, respectively. The results demonstrated the achievement of the highest percentage of mean Intersection Over Union (IOU), with an impressive 80.89% for brain tumor segmentation. These results outperformed other existing methods. The proposed model exhibits the potential to reduce manual segmentation time and subjectivity while enhancing the accuracy of brain tumor diagnosis, treatment planning, and disease monitoring. This research contributes to the field by addressing the problem of brain tumor detection and showcasing the promising results attained using deep learning techniques.

articleTitle: Temporal Fusion Transformer for Multi Horizon Bitcoin Price Forecasting
abstract: Bitcoin is one of the cryptocurrencies that have a large number of holders and a high transaction volume. Its price has experienced major fluctuation since its inception, resulting in relatively high price volatility. This has been a challenge for researchers over the past decade in forecasting its future price. In this study, we aim to address this problem by utilizing a neural network model called the Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT). The TFT model uses the concept of multi-horizon forecasting to learn from historical data and predict future prices based on multiple time steps. Due to the numerous factors influencing Bitcoin's price, our study incorporates additional predictive data, such as Twitter sentiment, trends, and seasonality. The proposed method is trained using the TFT model with historical Bitcoin data from 2014 until 2020, then we performed transfer learning by using different past covariates as inputs. As a result, the proposed method in this study demonstrated the best performance, with a MAE of 0.05, a RMSE of 0.07, a MAPE of 5.92%, and a quantile loss of 0.03, surpassing other approaches. This makes it the state-of-the-art solution for highly volatile forecasting using a neural network model.

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis of Skincare Product Reviews in Indonesian Language using IndoBERT and LSTM
abstract: This research focuses on analyzing sentiment to- wards skincare products in the Indonesian language, employing the IndoBERT approach and LSTM classification. The study aims to provide consumers with accurate information before purchasing skincare products and assist companies in improving product quality based on customer feedback. The method entails feature extraction with IndoBERT and classification using LSTM. The evaluation demonstrates excellent performance, with accu- racy reaching a value of 92.6%, indicating the effectiveness of the IndoBERT and LSTM approaches in sentiment classification for Indonesian skincare product reviews. These results lay a strong foundation for further development in sentiment analysis and contribute to the advancement of natural language processing technology in the context of skincare products in the Indonesian language.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Multi-label SINTANUR Rice Seed Classification Based on Deep Learning
abstract: Rice Seeds (Oryza sativa) are currently certified by BPSBTPH (Balai Pengawasan dan Sertifikasi Benih Tanaman Pangan dan Hortikultura) based on their germination rate. This process requires manual inspection by researchers and takes a considerable amount of time. To address this issue, this research proposes rice seed classification CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) models using our proposed models as STR- Net (SINTANUR-Neural Network). The model is constructed to classifying paddy rice seeds with multi-labels by growth dataset withdays 3, 5, 7, and 14 and the rice seed quality normal, abnormal, fresh, and dead categories. The result from the growth dataset yields accuracy rates of 96% on day 5, 94% on day 7, and 91% on day 14 when utilizing the STR-Net architecture. On the other hand, the ResNet50v2 architecture achieves accuracy rates of 98% on day 5, 97% on day 7, and 92% on day 14 with fixed hyperparameters. In addition, the accuracy of STR-Net model generated from the Quality dataset. The accuracy of the predictions obtained from the STR-Net models is satisfactory, reaching 92.59%, while the ResNet50v2 model achieves a slightly higher accuracy of 92.84%.

articleTitle: Analyzing Restaurants in Tourism Destinations Through Online Reviews Using Topic Modeling and Sentiment Analysis
abstract: This paper proposes a comprehensive methodology to analyze restaurants and tourism destinations. The methodology discovers the important aspects of the restaurants from online reviews using Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA). Parameter-tuning steps are presented to select the thresholds of the too-frequent and too-rare words, as well as the parameters related to bigram identification. The number of topics in LDA is selected based on the highest coherence score. Analyzing restaurant reviews from five super-priority tourism destinations in Indonesia (i.e., Borobudur, Lake Toba, Likupang, Labuan Bajo, and Mandalika), seven topics are identified, i.e., Experience, Taste-Value, Food & ItalianAmbience, Beach-Bar, Service, and Coffee-Pastry. Sentiment analysis is subsequently performed to evaluate each destination's restaurants. The analysis utilizes part-of-speech tagging, dependency tree parsing, and SenticNet5 lexicon. The restaurants in Mandalika averagely earned the most positive sentiment in all aspects. The accuracies of identified aspects and sentiments are almost 90%. The restaurants are then clustered based on the sentiments using the k-means method. The restaurants and policymakers may utilize the results to obtain specific ideas for improvements and promotions.

articleTitle: Android – Based Smart Nutrition Application for Children Nutritional Awareness
abstract: Malnutrition in children has emerged as a critical public health concern in the modern era, with significant implications for their long-term health and well-being. Lack of proper nutrition knowledge and awareness among parents often contributes to this issue. While prior research has created food identification systems to help people know the food nutrition, there is a glaring lack of applications expressly made to help parents understand their children's nutrition. To address this gap, we propose a smart nutrition application that aims to provide parents with essential information about the nutritional content of their children's food, thereby increasing their awareness and understanding of nutrition. The application's main feature utilizes an AI camera equipped with the You Only Look Once (YOLO) algorithm, enabling it to scan a meal and display detailed nutrient information. Furthermore, a UI-based and text-based ingredients calculator is provided to help parents calculate calories and food nutrition. Moreover, the article feature is intended to serve as a resource for parents to gain knowledge about children's nutrition. By leveraging TensorFlow, a machine learning framework, the proposed application achieves efficient and accurate food recognition with an overall accuracy rate of 90%.

articleTitle: Risk Score Estimation of Vulnerabilities Within VulnOS2 Using AlienVault Based on MITRE ATT&CK Model
abstract: Various vulnerabilities can weaken a computer network system. In dealing with these vulnerabilities, several tools are used to identify vulnerabilities so that in the future some preventive measures can be taken. This study compares the risk of vulnerabilities in VulnOS2. Vulnerabilities are identified from the vulnerability scan using AlienVault. The risk of vulnerabilities is then calculated using the risk estimation formula. The risk score estimation for vulnerability is classified into the MITRE ATT&CK matrix. The result shows that the highest risk score estimation is owned by Drupal Core Critical Remote Code Execution vulnerability which the risk score estimation is 202.5 and the lowest one is in SSH Weak Encryption Algorithms Supported which the risk score estimation is 26. Those vulnerabilities are classified in the ATT&CK Enterprise matrix to define in which ATT&CK Enterprise matrix categories the attack in vulnerabilities took place.

articleTitle: Fast Collaboration Competencies Model for Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC)
abstract: Some existing Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) models exist, such as Waterfall, Spiral, V-Model, Iterative, Big Bang, Agile, and others. SDLC as a framework based on the literature review has six (6) critical problems and weaknesses: poor documentation structures, lack of flexibility, inadequate analysis, confusion in selecting the right SDLC, unsuitable architecture, and lack of adaptability. To overcome the weaknesses of the SDLC, researchers have conducted various studies but have not found satisfactory results. This research aims to propose a novel SDLC model called the Fast Collaboration Competencies (FCC) model to make a better SDLC process. The novelties of this model contain three essential things: fast, collaboration, and competencies. The research produced a Novel FCC for the SDLC process and a list of advantages and disadvantages of the proposed Novel FCC. This research significantly contributes to software development by providing theoretical understanding, practical guidance, and enhanced team dynamics. The FCC model can reduce project delays, improve productivity, and increase customer satisfaction. By sharing findings, industry professionals can prioritize collaboration and teamwork, contributing to ongoing improvement and evolution of software development practices.

articleTitle: Impulsivity Level of a Potential Leader Based on Barin Signal Amplitude and Latency with the SVM Method
abstract: In making decisions, a leader must be based on consideration. In the selection of a leader, it is feared that the elected candidate has impulsivity that affects his performance as a leader. Everything related to impulsive behavior is directly related to brain activity. Therefore, by measuring brain activity with electroencephalography (EEG) equipment, The experiment was conducted at the Army Training Center in a room that had been conditioned away from the noise and provided comfort to the subject. The subject is in a relaxed state, opening his eyes while looking at the stimulus. Electroencephalography (EEG) was recorded using the Mitsar EEG-202.
